title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π = Π_{0,3}^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Π^~ ≃ Π·{1,τ_0} is an extension by an involution τ_0 (orbifold/S_3 symmetries); ρ and σ_∞ are fixed symmetry automorphisms. M_{0,3}^{!~} is Grothendieck's group of 'automorphismes à lacets': automorphisms of Π that send each inertia generator to a conjugate of a power of itself, compatibly with the symmetries. This is his own pre-Drinfeld version of GT^. To each u he attaches invariants f, g, h, α_0, β_0, α, β, ξ, η, which are the conjugating elements (to be determined) in u(l_i) ≈ conj·l_i^λ·conj^{-1}. α_0 and α only live in Π^~.

Previous page. Replacing u by int(γ)∘u gives f' = fγ^{-1}, g' = γ g ρ(γ)^{-1}, h' = γ h σ_∞(γ)^{-1}, α_0' = γα_0, β_0' = γβ_0, while α and β are unchanged. So α and β depend only on the outer class of u. Grothendieck states this as the reason to prefer the triple (α, β, f).

This page: composition law for u'' = u'u.
- g'' = u'(g) g'
- h'' = u'(h) h'
- f'' = f' u'(f)
- α_0'' = u'(α_0) α_0'
- β_0'' = u'(β_0) β_0'
- α'' = (f'u')(α)·α', where f'u' means int(f')∘u'
- β'' = (f'u')(β)·β'

The margin note handles α_0 and α, which lie in Π^~. Then u'(α_0) only makes sense literally when α_0 ∈ Π, i.e. when μ ≡ 1 (mod 3) by (52). Otherwise the formula must be interpreted through the natural extension of u' to Π^~.

Viewed as functions M_{0,3}^{!~} → Π^ (or Π^~), the maps f, g^{-1}, h^{-1}, α_0^{-1}, β_0^{-1} are 1-cocycles (crossed homomorphisms) for the tautological action of M on Π. The maps α^{-1} and β^{-1} are cocycles only on the subgroup where f = 1, i.e. the automorphisms normalizing L_0 = l_0^{Ẑ}.

Caveat. f is defined only up to the centralizer L_0 of l_0. This forces simultaneous ambiguities f ↦ l_0^n f, α ↦ l_0^n α, β ↦ l_0^n β. To make these canonical cocycles, Grothendieck proposes introducing a gerbe: an extension of M_{0,3}^{!~} by Ẑ, modelled on the 'special Teichmüller gerbes', on which f, α, β are unambiguous. He does not carry this out.

The next page pushes everything to GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 via Π_{0,3} ↪ PSL_2. There the determinants of α_0 and α equal ε_3 ≡ χ (mod 3).
errors: No genuine error found. I checked the stated composition rules against the inner-automorphism formulas (49) in the special case u' = int(γ); they are consistent, e.g. f'' = γ^{-1}·γfγ^{-1} = fγ^{-1}. The asymmetric conventions (f on the left, g on the right) suggest f is defined via u(l_0) = f^{-1} l_0^λ f, and g, h via a twisted (ρ, σ_∞) convention.
Minor gap, flagged by Grothendieck himself: for α_0 and α in Π^~ \ Π, the expression u'(α_0) needs u' extended to Π^~; the margin note acknowledges this.
The cocycle claim for f, α, β holds only modulo the L_0-ambiguity, as he notes.

ideas.what: Composition law for the invariants of loop-preserving automorphisms of π̂_1(P^1 − 3 points): f'' = f'·u'(f) and analogues, i.e. the group law of a GT^-type group expressed through crossed homomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Group law of Ĝ T (Drinfeld's (λ,f)·(λ',f') multiplication); f as a 1-cocycle on GT^ with values in F̂_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1990s) for the profinite version
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The explicit formulas are in these unpublished Longue Marche continuation notes.

ideas.what: α and β depend only on the outer class of u (invariant under int(γ)); preferring them to (g, h) or (α_0, β_0)
ideas.modern_name: Outer-automorphism invariants; normalization of GT elements modulo inner automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld/Ihara (normalizing f in the commutator subgroup)

ideas.what: Resolving the inertia ambiguity f ↦ l_0^n f by a gerbe extending M_{0,3}^{!~} by Ẑ, modelled on 'special Teichmüller gerbes'
ideas.modern_name: Central extension or gerbe lifting the action to a tangential-basepoint / Teichmüller-groupoid setting. Comparable to Deligne–Ihara tangential base points, or Drinfeld's commutator-subgroup normalization of f.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tangential base points: Deligne (1989), Ihara; normalization of f: Drinfeld (1990)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes to remove the l_0^n ambiguity of (f, α, β) by building a Ẑ-gerbe over his group of loop-automorphisms, modelled on Teichmüller gerbes, so that f, α^{-1}, β^{-1} become canonical cocycles. He leaves this undone. The modern literature removes the ambiguity differently: Drinfeld requires f to lie in the commutator subgroup, and Ihara/Nakamura use tangential base points. A gerbe-theoretic version of this rigidification does not seem to have been written down.
missed.quote: il faudrait introduire une gerbe extension de M_{0,3}^{!~} par Ẑ, sur la modèle des gerbes de Teichmüller spéciaux, sur laquelle f, α, β soient définis
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a stacky/gerbe formulation of the GT normalization. Such a formulation could clarify how the choice of tangential base point is a trivialization of a Ẑ-gerbe, and could connect to the Teichmüller tower and to stack-theoretic treatments of GT^.

deep.surprise_reason: These are mostly routine cocycle bookkeeping for what is essentially Grothendieck's pre-Drinfeld GT^. It is historically interesting, given the probable early-1980s date, but the composition laws are now standard. The proposed Ẑ-gerbe rigidification is a small unfinished idea that is mildly novel in form.
transcription_corrections: The first formula in the right column is α'' = (f'u')(α)·α', not 'α'' = (f'(u')(α).α''; the asterisk marks the margin note.

Margin: 'ont un sens si α_0, α ∈ Π_{0,3} i.e. μ ≡ 1 (3), d'après (52)' — plausible reading. The remainder is roughly 'il n'y a aucune définition qui ait un sens pour u'(α_0)... mais la formule α_0'' = u'(α_0)α_0' garde un sens'.
'on considère f [?] comme variable' is better read as 'si on considère u comme variable dans M_{0,3}^{!~}'.
'un peu brutalement' is likely 'À vrai dire, ceci est un peu brutal / dit un peu brutalement'.
'sur la modèle des gerbes de Teichmüller spéciaux' should read 'sur le modèle des gerbes de Teichmüller spéciales'.
